about.title: Tustin Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a Tustin family loses someone to a preventable crash or another negligent act, the weeks that follow are about grief, not paperwork. Yet California gives certain survivors a way to seek accountability in civil court, and that path has its own rules. In 2025, Tustin recorded 328 injury collisions and five traffic deaths. The corridors with the most reported crashes are ones residents drive daily: I-5 northbound, Red Hill Avenue, Newport Avenue and Jamboree Road. A wrongful death claim in Orange County belongs first to a spouse or domestic partner and children; other dependents or heirs may qualify when those relatives are absent. Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. The deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and considerably shorter when a government entity is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect Tustin families, at no cost, with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency.

items.title: Clarity on Who Can File
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can confirm where your family stands before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines Handled Early
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is much shorter if a public entity is involved. Connecting early keeps those options open.

items.title: Every Category of Loss Considered
items.desc: Funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance are all recognized under California law. Contingency representation means no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: The crash happened on I-5 in Tustin rather than a city street. Does that change anything?
items.answer: It can. Freeways are maintained by the state, so if road conditions or design played a role, a government entity may be among the responsible parties. Claims against public entities in California carry a far shorter deadline than the standard two years, so it is worth speaking with an attorney soon.

items.question: There is a criminal case against the driver. Do we have to wait for it to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action, and it does not depend on a conviction. Many families pursue both at the same time, and the two-year civil deadline keeps running regardless of the criminal court's schedule.

items.question: My parent died and there is no surviving spouse. Can adult children bring the claim?
items.answer: Yes. Under California law, children have standing alongside a spouse or domestic partner, and when there is no spouse they are typically first in line. If there are no children either, certain dependents or heirs may qualify, which an attorney can sort out based on your family's situation.
